newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Candidate Menem says Argentina to be in world top 10.
newsitem.headline: Candidate Menem says Argentina to be in world top 10.

text.p: President Carlos Menem launched his Peronist Party's campaign for October's congressional elections by saying Argentina would be among the world's top 10 economies by 1999, reports said on Sunday.

Menem told 6,000 supporters in a rally at a sports stadium at the seaside city of Mar del Plata on Saturday night that the Radical Party and centre-left Frepaso alliance just "automatically get in the way of everything and never propose solutions," the La Nacion newspaper reported.

Menem promised that Argentina will enjoy rapid growth in the last years of his presidency. "Today, Argentina is number 17 in the world, and when I leave government it will be one of the 10 best-off countries on the planet," he said.
Many of the chanting supporters bore banners supporting a third Menem bid for the presidency when his term expires in 1999, even though the constitution limits presidents to a maximum of two terms.
But Menem succeeded during his first presidency in modifying the constitution that then permitted only one period in office.

Since taking power in 1989, Menem has presided over the defeat of hyperinflation, mass privatisations and the opening of the economy to international trade and investment. But unemployment has soared and more than one in six Argentines is without a job.
